section_summary.extract_value: This section reports construct and incremental validity evidence for the Dutch BAS-2. It states BAS-2 scores were positively correlated with appearance satisfaction, functionality satisfaction, self-esteem, and optimistic life orientation, and negatively correlated with self-objectification and BMI (Table 1). Hierarchical regressions showed BAS-2 scores made a significant incremental contribution to predicting self-esteem and optimistic life orientation (e.g., self-esteem model F(3, 306) = 103.67, R2 change .42 to .50; optimistic life orientation model F(3, 306) = 46.39, R2 change .29 to .31).
section_summary.evidence_source: Quoted sentences: "Dutch BAS-2 scores demonstrated good convergent validity: they were significantly positively correlated with appearance satisfaction, functionality satisfaction, self-esteem, and optimistic life orientation, and significantly negatively correlated with selfobjectification and BMI (Table 1)." and the regression result sentences beginning "For self-esteem, the final model proved significant, F(3, 306) = 103.67, R2 = .50, p < .001..." and "Regarding optimistic life orientation, the final model was significant, F(3, 306) = 46.39, R2 = .31, p < .001..."
